record.context_brief: Arbitrarily many balanced vertices from four boundary points
record.original_question: Do there exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with exactly four unbalanced vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices? The conjecture further suggests that this may already hold when the four unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2.2. There exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with 4 unbalanced vertices and an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. (Moreover, we will not be surprised if this assertion is already true in the case when the set of unbalanced vertices coincides with the set of vertices of a square).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A geodesic net in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a finite graph embedded in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose edges are straight line segments, together with a designated subset of its vertices called boundary (or unbalanced) vertices. A non-boundary vertex $v$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges emanating from $v$ equals the zero vector; every non-boundary vertex is required to be balanced. The boundary vertices are those at which the corresponding sum of unit tangent vectors is allowed to be nonzero.

Question: Does there exist, for every positive integer $N$, a geodesic net in $\mathbb{R}^2$ having exactly four unbalanced vertices and at least $N$ balanced vertices? In particular, does such a family exist in which the four unbalanced vertices are the four vertices of a square?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. A November 2025 preprint reports progress by constructing an irreducible geodesic net in the plane with four boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices (improving an earlier example with 16), and suggests the construction might generalize to give arbitrarily many balanced vertices, but does not prove the full conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a geodesic net in the plane with four boundary vertices and 25 balanced vertices, increasing the previously known maximum from 16 to 25, with potential for generalization.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work makes progress toward but does not yet resolve the conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the conjecture about existence of geodesic nets with 4 unbalanced vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is stated as an open problem.
